evaluation.mechanism: A test can omit a behavior or fail to transfer to relevant work; difference alone is not evidence of dangerous failure.
evaluation.conditions: A consequential difference in tasks, context or permissions must remain unaddressed by other tests and operational safeguards.
evaluation.counterexample: The retained prompted-model comparison and successful detection in covered settings rule out treating every monitor as ineffective.
evaluation.evidence: Reread the controlled monitor study, evaluation-method qualifications, developer card corrections and external-evaluation proposal.
evaluation.limits: Preserve limited status and indirect evidence. Neither classification AUROC nor an unimplemented audit proposal establishes an operational miss rate.
evaluation.mitigation: Retain unfamiliar test categories, alternative monitors, realistic settings and scrutiny of external evaluators’ actual access.
evaluation.readerContext: Both editions identify the AI doing the checking and distinguish that role from the AI whose work is checked.
evaluation.whyHere: This remains one possible route to C3a, alongside other monitoring failures, rather than a compulsory temporal stage.

finance.mechanism: Losses, funding demand or operational failures spread only when relevant buffers and responses fail to contain them.
finance.conditions: Retain the conjunction of F1, F2 and F4 in F1-F3 and the finance-conditions group; financial exposure alone does not establish a crisis.
finance.counterexample: Effective limits, available liquidity or continuity and recovery can localize a disturbance despite AI involvement and faulty actions.
finance.evidence: Reread the FSI policy-response discussion and FSB publication summaries; reviewed newer proposals as proposals, not outcome measurements.
finance.limits: Keep F4 hypothetical. Price movements, policy statements and a shared provider do not by themselves prove system-wide barrier failure.
finance.mitigation: Keep operational recovery separate from capital and liquidity; retain human control, service continuity and provider contingencies.
finance.readerContext: Japanese and English explain available funds, losses and payment continuity without requiring prior knowledge of financial regulation.
finance.whyHere: The finance route concerns impaired financial services and has additional conditions; it is not a direct path to money disappearing or extinction.

scope.mechanism: A dated recheck records an editorial decision to retain the explanations; it does not create a new measured outcome.
scope.conditions: Advance only C3a1, F4 and the inspected C3a1 evidence-summary date after the documented source comparison.
scope.counterexample: Other entries remain unchanged even when their linked index was visited; the map date is not a whole-map certification.
scope.evidence: The accompanying Markdown records primary passages, unchanged interpretations, candidates not incorporated and the scan boundary.
scope.limits: No new evidence class, node explanation, source date or probability is introduced. This is an editorial review, not independent peer review.
scope.mitigation: Keep the work isolated and draft, retain previous history by stable ID, and validate both language packages before requesting review.
scope.readerContext: The bilingual history states which entries were reviewed and why their text and classification were retained.
scope.whyHere: History and map metadata disclose the scoped maintenance decision without implying that a new research result was found.
